item.title: SC suggests Parliament to bring amendment to section 26E of SARFAESI Act
item.description: The Supreme Court on Thursday said Parliament should consider bringing an appropriate amendment to section 26E of the SARFAESI Act and that an explanation of the expression "all other debts" in the provision may be provided authoritatively. Section 26E of the SARFAESI Act, 2002, gives secured creditors priority to recover their debts ahead of other debts and government dues once a security interest is registered. A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and Ujjal Bhuyan made the suggestion while referring a legal question -- whether the "deposits" sought to be recovered under the Maharashtra Protection of Interest of Depositors (in Financial Establishments) Act would fall within the ambit of the expression "all other debts" appearing in section 26E of the SARFAESI Act -- to a three-judge bench. item.title: Exporters seek early trade deal with US, cite 17% tariff advantage
item.description: Indian exporters on Thursday urged the government to seal a trade pact with the US at the earliest, saying the proposed 17 per cent tariff, as outlined in the USTR report, would give India an advantage over competing nations. They said that this is the right time to finalise the deal as exporters are getting good orders from the US buyers. "India should do the trade deal as soon as possible. We are getting a lot of orders from the US, and further opening of the market will help increase exports," Federation of Indian Export Organisations (FIEO) President S C Ralhan said. He added that the absence of a trade deal with the US could hurt India's exports by putting domestic exporters at a disadvantage compared with competitors from countries that enjoy lower tariff rates. item.title: Maharashtra projects revenue deficit despite strong tax base, low debt: Rpt
item.description: Maharashtra has a relatively strong tax base and one of the country's lowest debt burdens, but has budgeted for a revenue deficit of 0.7 per cent of its Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP) in 2026-27, a report has said. The report by PRS Legislative Research notes that the state's own tax revenue, including state Goods and Services Tax (GST), stamp duty and VAT, is estimated at 7.7 per cent of its GSDP, higher than the average of seven per cent. Maharashtra's outstanding debt is below 20 per cent of its GSDP, in line with the recommendation of the FRBM Review Committee (2017). It is among only three states meeting this benchmark, the other two being Gujarat and Odisha. The state's fiscal deficit is budgeted at 2.6 per cent, also below the 16th Finance Commission's recommendation. The outstanding liabilities at the end of March 2026 are Rs 9 lakh crore and the GSDP is Rs 49.3 lakh crore as per 2025-26 budget estimate.
